Conventional therapies (“split” or
“mixed” dose) There are two basic 
conventional therapy regimens. Option
#1: Short- or rapid-acting insulin mixed
with intermediate-acting insulins1 given 
before breakfast and before evening
meal. Option #2: Combination of short- 
and intermediate-acting insulins before
breakfast, short-acting insulin before
evening meals, and intermediate-acting
insulin at bedtime. Used to control
dawn phenomenon.
Source: Adapted from: Tamborlane WV, Sikes KA,
Swan K, Weignzimer SA. Type 1 diabetes in children.
In American Diabetes Association. Therapy for 
Diabetes Mellitus and Related Disorders, 5th ed. Al-
exandria, VA: American Diabetes Association, 2009.
